label: Stop 6: The House with the Heads, Keizersgracht 123

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. We're on the canal. And look at that.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Look up. Six stone heads, set into the facade, just under the roof line.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: They're staring.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: They are. This is the Huis met de Hoofden.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The House with the Heads. Keizersgracht 123.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So, what are they?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The record first. The house was built in 1622, for a wealthy merchant and art lover named Nicolaas Sohier.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The facade is attributed to Hendrick de Keyser.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: But he died in 1621, so it was probably finished by his son, Pieter de Keyser.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Wait. The same De Keyser from the Zuiderkerk.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The same. Good callback.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I notice things.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The six heads are Roman gods. Each has a clue.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Apollo has a laurel wreath, for the arts.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Ceres has grain, for agriculture.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Mercury has a winged helmet, for trade.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Minerva stands for wisdom. Bacchus has grapes, for wine.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And Diana has a half moon, for the hunt.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So it's an art collector's house, decorated with gods.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Yes. That's the record.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the legend?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Here it is. It's the story told on the canal after dark.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Six burglars broke into the house.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A maid, alone, caught them, and cut off their heads.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The six heads on the wall are the thieves.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Oh, that's grim. And a bit satisfying.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Careful. It's a legend. The record is the gods.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Legend. Stamp it.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Stamped. We found no source that supports it.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's the kind of story a house with six faces collects.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And since it's Halloween, can I say one thing?

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: The gods are looking at us.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You may. That's atmosphere. Not fact.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Who lived here?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: After Sohier, a man named Louis de Geer bought it in 1634, and his family held it for four generations.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Later owners included Anthoni Grill, who rented it from 1752 to 1775.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In 1811, Cornelis Sebille Roos settled here.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The city restored it in 1907.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And now?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It houses the Embassy of the Free Mind, a museum and cultural platform.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's connected to a library of hermetic philosophy, the Bibliotheca Philosophica Hermetica.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The buyer announced in 2006 was Joost Ritman.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A library of mystery. In a house of heads.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It does fit.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay, final tally?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Legends: the weeping wives, the miracle's details, Cornelia's gutter burial, and the six thieves.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Everything else in the walk is record.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Four legends, and a heap of real history.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the real history was spookier.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Often is.
